# Checkout

Fetches all unread GitHub notifications and presents them as a prioritised, scannable inbox — without opening a browser.

Usage: `/checkout`

---

## Step 1 — Fetch all unread notifications

```bash
gh api /notifications?all=false&per_page=100 --paginate
```

This returns all unread notifications across every repo you have access to.

---

## Step 1.5 — Filter to last 7 days

After fetching, filter out notifications older than 7 days using `updated_at`. Use the current date (today) to calculate. Discard anything from before 7 days ago.

---

## Step 2 — Convert API URLs to web URLs

Each notification's `subject.url` is an API URL. Convert to a human-usable web URL:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/pulls/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/releases/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/tag/...` (use `repository.html_url/releases`)
- For anything else: use `https://github.com/<repository.full_name>`

---

## Step 3 — Classify and prioritise

Use the `reason` field to assign a priority tier:

**🔴 Needs your action**
- `review_requested` — someone asked you to review a PR
- `mention` — you were @mentioned
- `team_mention` — your team was @mentioned
- `assign` — you were assigned to an issue or PR
- `security_alert` — security vulnerability detected

**🟡 FYI / follow-up**
- `comment` — new comment on something you're involved in
- `state_change` — issue or PR you follow changed state (closed, merged…)
- `author` — activity on something you created

**⚪ Low priority (subscribed noise)**
- `subscribed` — activity on a repo you watch
- `manual` — something you manually subscribed to
- `your_activity` — triggered by your own actions

---

## Step 4 — Output the inbox

Open with a bold stats banner. Compute an urgency bar where each block represents 5% of total notifications that need attention (🔴 + 🟡 combined). Use `█` for filled and `░` for empty, across 20 characters total.

**📬 GitHub Inbox** — {Weekday D Month YYYY}

🔴 **{N} urgent**  ·  🟡 **{N} fyi**  ·  ⚪ {N} noise  ·  {total} total
Urgency  {progress_bar}  {pct}% need attention
```

Then a horizontal rule: `---`

---

### 🔴 Urgent tier

Render the section header as:
```
### 🔴 Needs Your Action — {N} notifications
```

Group by repo. For each repo:
```
**📂 owner/repo** · {N}
```
Then list notifications in tree style — use `├` for all items except the last which gets `└`. Each item is one line:

```
├ {icon}  [{Title — max 68 chars}]({web_url})  `{label}` · *{age}*
└ {icon}  [{Title — max 68 chars}]({web_url})  `{label}` · *{age}*
```

Separate repos with a blank line.

---

Render the section header as:
```
### 🟡 FYI / Follow-up — {N} notifications
```

Same tree style per-repo as above.

---

One-liner only:
```
### ⚪ Low Priority — {N} items skipped

---

### ⚪ Low Priority — 3 items skipped

Generates a standup update from your GitHub activity feed, covering every repo you touched.

```bash

```

This returns up to 90 days of events across all repos. Filter to the target date. Relevant event types:

| Type | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| `PushEvent` | Commits pushed to a branch |
| `PullRequestEvent` | PR opened, closed, merged, or ready for review |
| `PullRequestReviewEvent` | PR review submitted |
| `PullRequestReviewCommentEvent` | Inline review comment |
| `IssueCommentEvent` | Comment on an issue or PR |

Fair enough — the tree characters and heavy emoji don't actually render with any visual weight in markdown, so it just looks like noisy plain text. The design looked good on paper but fights against what markdown can actually do in chat.

What *does* render well in markdown:

- **Tables** → actual grid layout
- **Code blocks** → monospace with background
- **H3/H4 headers** → real visual hierarchy
- **Bold** → actual weight
- **Horizontal rules** → clean dividers

The `├`, `└`, progress bars, and box-drawing chars all land as flat Unicode — no visual benefit.
